title: Realistic tenant-mix dissector and customer SLA safeguard
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build a repeatable bench and acceptance workflow that reproduces realistic multi-tenant mixes and validates Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees and autoscaler safety guards. This ticket covers: (1) a tenant-mix "dissector" that synthesizes traffic from customer traces into labeled load profiles (short bursts, sustained workloads, tail-traffics, cold-cache sessions), (2) an execution harness that runs deterministic ramp/sustain/drain scenarios across an isolated Dedicated pool and collects latency/cost/fallback metrics, and (3) a curated customer acceptance checklist and runbook that Solutions/SEs can run against customer-provisioned Dedicated clusters for sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: Dissector can convert three anonymized production trace samples into parametrized load recipes (burst-heavy, long-session, mixed-tenancy) reproducibly
Harness executes ramp->sustain->drain scenarios with configurable tenant weighting and injects KV cache cold-starts with seedable RNG
Collected metrics include p50/p90/p95/p99/p999 latency, tail token throughput, autoscaler decision timestamps, node utilization, and per-tenant error rates
Automated pass/fail rules flag SLO violations (p99 <= target, sustained throughput >= committed baseline) and generate an opinionated remediation list
Customer acceptance checklist produced and validated with Solutions Engineering on two pilot customers (internal sign-off recorded)
Runbook includes exact CLI commands, required IAM roles, Confluence links, and a teardown procedure to avoid cross-tenant contamination
steps: Collect three anonymized trace samples from existing Dedicated customers (work with Security & Legal to sign off PII removal)
Implement trace parser that extracts session lengths, request size distribution, KV cache hit sequences, and inter-arrival times
Design tenant-mix parametrization schema (weights, session types, cold-start frequency, richness factor) and store as JSON recipes
Extend existing load driver to accept recipe files and tag requests with opaque tenant IDs for per-tenant metrics
Add autoscaler event hooks to record scale decision context (metrics that triggered scale up/down and cooldown windows)
Run bench in isolation on a staging Dedicated pool, iterate to tune ramp durations to avoid thrashing the autoscaler
Produce per-run artifact bundle: raw logs, parsed metrics CSV, Grafana dashboard link, opinionated pass/fail report
Create customer-facing acceptance checklist and one-page executive summary for Solutions Engineering
metrics: sustained token throughput (tokens/s) per tenant and aggregate
node GPU utilization and memory pressure
autoscaler actions: timestamped scale events and delta nodes
cache warmup curve: first-request latency vs. after-n requests
error rate and class breakdown (4xx, 5xx, model-timeouts)
tradeoffs_and_notes: We deliberately avoid trying to perfectly emulate every customer; aim is to surface regressions and autoscaler misbehavior by using a small set of orthogonal recipes
Heavy replay of production traces can overfit to current kernel selection; include lightweight randomized perturbation to detect brittle heuristics
Autoscaler cooldowns: shorter cooldowns expose more agility but increase risk of oscillation. We'll parameterize cooldown to test both conservative and responsive configs

Per-tenant isolation: tagging requests with opaque tenant IDs is sufficient for metrics but we must ensure no data leakage — Security review required for trace ingestion pipeline (Legal already looped)
Harness will run in a fenced staging Dedicated pool to avoid customer impact; capacity for long sustain runs will be scheduled to minimize cloud cost
